title: fix(core): restore AST fidelity for headings, titles and reference links

commits.message:
fix(core): keep heading text for setext and closed ATX headings `headingTextRange` was written for the ATX shape only: skip the leading `HeaderMark` run, then trim a trailing one. Both heading forms use the same `HeaderMark` node name, so that walk misreads the other two layouts: - setext (`title\n=====`) has a single mark — the underline, *after* the text. It was skipped as the opening mark and trimmed as the closing mark, leaving `cursor` past `end` and an empty range. - closed ATX (`## title ##`) puts the heading text in raw source rather than a child node, so both marks are adjacent siblings. The leading `while` consumed them both and pushed `cursor` to the node end. Either way `depth` and `position` stayed correct while `children` came out empty, so the damage surfaced in AST consumers rather than in the editor: unlabeled outline entries (an accessible-name failure), short word counts, and `exportHTML()` emitting `

`. Split the two forms apart instead of sharing one walk, and take a single node at each end rather than looping. `lezer-helpers` already maps `SetextHeading1/2` to a depth, so setext was meant to work — this restores the text to match.

fix(core): read link and image titles instead of hardcoding null

`title` was pinned to `null` on every Link and Image, even though Lezer
already exposes the title as a `LinkTitle` child. CommonMark permits three
delimiter forms — `"…"`, `'…'`, `(…)` — so read the child and strip whichever
pair it carries, collapsing an empty title to `null` the way remark does.

Destinations get the same treatment: the `<…>` form exists so a url can
contain spaces, and the brackets are delimiters rather than part of the url.

`adaptLinkReference` re-parsed the definition line with one regex,
`/^\[([^\]]+)\]:\s*(\S+)(?:\s+"([^"]*)")?/`, which lost three things the node
tree already had right — `\S+` truncated an angle-bracketed url at the first
space, only the double-quoted title form matched, and `identifier` kept the
author's casing where mdast case-folds it so `[Foo]` resolves against
`[foo]: …`. Read the `LinkLabel` / `URL` / `LinkTitle` children instead.

`live-preview-table.ts` already reads `node.title`, so it benefits directly.

fix(core): emit linkReference and imageReference for reference links

`[text][ref]`, `[text][]` and `[text]` all came out as `{type:"link"}` with
the whole raw source as the url, so `[full][ref]` exported as
`<a href="[full][ref]">` — a dead link — and the editor published the same
string as `data-link-url` while hiding none of the brackets, since the node
fell through to the GFM bare-URL branch.

mdast models these as separate node types: the destination stays in the
companion `definition`, and the reference carries `identifier` / `label` /
`referenceType` for the renderer to resolve. Classify the three forms off the
`LinkLabel` child and emit `linkReference`, with `imageReference` as the
`![alt][ref]` counterpart. `plugin-wordcount` already handled both types,
which is a good sign they were always the intended output.

The label walk that Link used moves into `readLinkLabelChildren` so
references share it and keep nested marks — `[**bold**][ref]` stays a Strong.

Changing the node type means the decoration path has to follow, or the
editor silently stops rendering reference links: `linkReference` joins the
`LivePreviewNode` union and the `isLivePreviewNode` allowlist, and
`getInlineMarkerStyle` gains a case that hides the brackets without
attaching a url it does not have.

One known deviation from remark, documented on `readReference`: CommonMark
demands a matching definition and falls back to literal text otherwise.
Checking that needs all definitions up front, turning this adapter's single
pass into two, and staying cheap enough for the live-preview hot path is why
it exists — so an undefined reference is still emitted as a `linkReference`.
